note: Development design only. No with-skill/without-skill run has been executed for this version; do not cite these cases as measured uplift.

release_holdout.reason: These cases are public in the package and readable by implementers. A release holdout must be controlled outside the authoring context.

evals.prompt: Add a row to my Notion 'Vendors' database for Acme Corp, status Active, tag it 'hardware'. If Acme is already in there, just update it. Here's the database URL: https://notion.so/ws/Vendors-215d872b594c81bdbea20002d0d66c12
evals.fixtures: Fetched database returns one data source; schema has title property 'Vendor', status 'State' with options Active/Inactive, multi_select 'Tags'. One existing row titled 'Acme Corp'.
evals.output_contract: Resolved data source, upsert outcome, exact properties written, re-fetch confirmation.

expectations.text: Response resolves the database's `data_sources[]` and targets a `data_source_id`, not the bare database ID, before any schema or row call.
Response writes the title using the fetched property name `Vendor`, not an assumed `Name` or `Title`.
Response queries for an existing match and reports the operation as an update of the existing Acme Corp row, not a new create.
Response writes the status as `{"status": {"name": "Active"}}` using the schema's exact option name.

evals.prompt: Create a row in the Projects data source with Name 'Atlas', Budget 50000, link it to the client 'Northwind' (database id 9a1b...), and set Priority to High.
evals.fixtures: Schema has title 'Name', number 'Budget', relation 'Client' targeting a data source; there is no 'Priority' property.
evals.output_contract: Create plan that rejects unsupported fields and uses a valid relation payload.

expectations.text: Response states that `Priority` is not in the fetched schema and that adding it is a schema change, rather than dropping it silently or inventing the property.
Response does not send `database_id` in the relation write and uses only page IDs scoped to the related data source.
Response runs or cites `scripts/validate_row_payload.py` against the fetched schema before sending the write.
Response does not report the row as created with Priority set.

evals.prompt: Upsert these 2,400 contacts from my CSV into the Contacts database, matching on email. Also, there are two existing rows for jane@example.com, just pick one.
evals.fixtures: Prompt-only scenario. Two existing rows share the email key.
evals.output_contract: Scope boundary for volume and an explicit stop on the ambiguous key.

expectations.text: Response states that a multi-thousand-row load is outside this skill and routes to a bulk-data-ops capability rather than running 2,400 sequential row writes.
Response refuses to silently pick one of the two jane@example.com rows and asks which one, or whether a new row is intended.
Response names the 100-item per-request cap for multi_select, relation, or people writes when describing chunking.
Response does not archive or delete a duplicate row and names `okhp3-notion-destructive-ops` as the owner of any removal.
